content.title: Fixpoint Theory en Biworlds: De Kracht van Benaderingen in Kennisrepresentatie
content.abstract: Approximations arise in almost every scientific field and application: either by design, to allow for certain constructions or to make an otherwise too complicated problem more tractable; or by lack of information, like in the case of predictions, and empirical measurements. Thus, formally representing and being able to use this kind of incomplete information is fundamental. In the context of Knowledge Representation and Reasoning, this is achieved through various devices, like partially defined functions and objects, or three- and four-valued semantics. In this thesis, we explore and showcase
